items.value: Both statements are correct, and the absence of any hard-asset backing is precisely why bondholders could not enforce payment in a default
items.reasoning: Statement-II is plainly correct: since the end of the gold standard, United States Treasury securities carry no collateral of any kind and rest only on the 'full faith and credit' of the US Government. Statement-I follows directly from that: because there is no pledged asset and a sovereign cannot be compelled to pay, holders of a defaulted Treasury Bond have no property to proceed against and no mechanism to enforce their claim — the claim survives as a promise but cannot be exercised. That is exactly the causal link Statement-II supplies, so the explanation relation holds and B is excluded. Runner-up is D, which would win if the examiner treats Statement-I as false on the ground that a US default would in practice be technical and temporary, with bondholders still holding a legally valid claim that is eventually honoured; on that stricter reading only Statement-II survives.

items.value: Statement-I is correct (syndication spreads default risk across lenders) but Statement-II is wrong — a syndicated facility can perfectly well be a revolving credit line
items.reasoning: Spreading a single large borrower's default risk across a group of lenders, none of whom has to carry the whole exposure, is the defining purpose of syndicated lending, so Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is false: syndicated facilities are routinely structured as revolving credit lines as well as lump-sum term loans, and a single syndicated agreement often contains both a term tranche and a revolver. Because Statement-II is incorrect, A and B are excluded, and D is excluded because Statement-I is sound.

items.value: Statements 1, 2 and 4 — the digital rupee is sovereign currency aligned to monetary policy, sits as a liability on the RBI balance sheet, and is freely convertible against bank money and cash; it is not inflation-proof
items.reasoning: The RBI's own description of a central bank digital currency has three of these built in: it is sovereign currency issued in alignment with monetary policy (1), it appears as a liability on the central bank's balance sheet (2), and it must be freely convertible against commercial bank money and cash (4). Statement 3 is the odd one out — the digital rupee is simply the rupee in digital form, so it carries exactly the same exposure to inflation as cash; nothing in its design indexes or insures its value. Since 3 is false and 4 is true, only the combination 1, 2 and 4 survives.

items.value: Only Shakyamuni and Tathagata are epithets of the Buddha; Nayaputta belongs to Mahavira
items.reasoning: Shakyamuni ('sage of the Shakya clan') and Tathagata ('thus-gone/thus-come', the Buddha's own habitual self-designation in the Pali suttas) are both standard epithets of Gautama Buddha. Nayaputta (Nataputta, Sanskrit Jnatriputra, 'son of the Jnatrika clan') is the clan-name by which the Buddhist texts themselves refer to Nigantha Nataputta, that is Mahavira, the Jaina teacher — not to the Buddha. So statement 1 fails and only 2 and 3 stand.

items.value: Only rows 2 (Inamgaon, Maharashtra, Chalcolithic) and 3 (Mangadu, Kerala, megalithic) are correctly matched
items.reasoning: Row 1 fails on the State: Chandraketugarh, the early historic trading and port town on the Bidyadhari, is in North 24 Parganas district of West Bengal, not Odisha. Row 2 is correct — Inamgaon on the Ghod river in Pune district is the type-site of the Jorwe phase of the Chalcolithic in Maharashtra. Row 3 is correct — Mangadu in Kollam district, Kerala, is a well-known megalithic burial site. Row 4 fails on the description: Salihundam in Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh is a hilltop Buddhist complex of stupas, chaityas and viharas, not a group of rock-cut cave shrines (those in Andhra are at sites such as Guntupalli and Sankaram). With 1 and 4 out, only the pair 2 and 3 remains.

items.value: Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara permitted the Portuguese to build a fort at Bhatkal
items.reasoning: Bhatkal on the Kanara coast lay within Vijayanagara territory, and Krishnadevaraya cultivated the Portuguese under Albuquerque as suppliers of Arabian horses and as a counterweight to Bijapur; in the course of that understanding he granted them permission to build a fort at Bhatkal. Narasimha Saluva died in 1491, before the Portuguese reached India in 1498, so B is chronologically impossible. Muhammad Shah III was a Bahmani sultan of the late fifteenth century, again pre-Portuguese, and Yusuf Adil Shah of Bijapur was the ruler the Portuguese fought at Goa rather than one who granted them a coastal fort.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — the Permanent Settlement's sunset clause cost a defaulting zamindar his zamindari; the Ryotwari system gave no such exemption in bad years
items.reasoning: Statement 2 is correct and describes the 'Sunset Law' of the Permanent Settlement of 1793: if the fixed revenue was not paid by sunset of the appointed day, the estate was put to public auction and the zamindar lost his zamindari, which is why so many old Bengal families were displaced within a generation. Statement 1 is false as printed — the Ryotwari settlement's standing criticism is precisely that the assessment was pitched high and collected rigidly from the individual ryot even when the harvest failed, with no built-in exemption for bad seasons or natural calamity. It is worth flagging that the stem itself is loose: Cornwallis had nothing to do with the Ryotwari settlement, which was introduced in Madras by Read and Munro and in Bombay by Elphinstone, so statement 1 is doubly out of place. Runner-up is C, which would win if the examiner credits the theoretical advantage claimed for Ryotwari — that being a temporary, periodically revised settlement made directly with the cultivator, it permitted remission of revenue in years of crop failure, unlike the fixed Permanent Settlement demand.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct — the Upanishads do predate the Puranas, but they are full of parables
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is false: the Upanishads teach very largely through parable and narrative — Nachiketa and Yama in the Katha, Satyakama Jabala and the Svetaketu 'salt dissolved in water' episode in the Chandogya, the contest of the gods and demons, the Yajnavalkya-Gargi and Yajnavalkya-Maitreyi dialogues in the Brihadaranyaka. Statement 2 is correct: the principal Upanishads belong to the later Vedic period, roughly the eighth to fifth centuries BCE, whereas the Puranas in their surviving form are compiled from about the early centuries CE onwards. So only 2 stands.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct — India is a member of the International Grains Council, but membership is in no way a condition for trading in rice or wheat
items.reasoning: India is a member of the London-based International Grains Council, the intergovernmental body set up under the Grains Trade Convention to monitor the world grain market and promote cooperation in grain trade, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is plainly false: the IGC is an information and cooperation forum with no licensing power, and grain exports and imports are governed by national trade policy and WTO obligations, not by IGC membership — many active grain traders are not members at all.

items.value: Garba of Gujarat, inscribed in 2023, is the latest of the four on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list
items.reasoning: Ordering the four by year of inscription: Chhau dance 2010, Kumbh Mela 2017, Durga Puja in Kolkata 2021, and Garba of Gujarat 2023. Garba is therefore the most recent of the four to be added to the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

items.value: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the provisional (temporary) President of the Constituent Assembly
items.reasoning: When the Constituent Assembly met for the first time on 9 December 1946, Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, as its oldest member, was chosen temporary or provisional President in accordance with French practice. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, not the Assembly; Rajagopalachari and T. T. Krishnamachari held no such presiding office in the Assembly.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct — the Act provided for an All India Federation of Provinces and Princely States, but Defence and External Affairs were reserved to the Governor-General, not the federal legislature
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Government of India Act, 1935 provided for an All India Federation comprising the British Indian Provinces and such Princely States as chose to accede, though the federation never came into being because too few States acceded. Statement 2 is false: the Act introduced dyarchy at the Centre, under which Defence, External Affairs, ecclesiastical affairs and tribal areas were 'reserved' subjects to be administered by the Governor-General with the help of counsellors not responsible to the legislature — the very opposite of being under the control of the federal legislature.

items.value: Madhyama-vyayoga is a play attributed to Bhasa
items.reasoning: The thirteen plays recovered in the Trivandrum manuscripts and attributed to the playwright Bhasa include Madhyama-vyayoga, a one-act vyayoga drawn from the Mahabharata, alongside Svapnavasavadatta, Urubhanga, Karnabhara, Pancharatra and Dutavakya. The other three options are not plays at all and belong to other authors: Kavyalankara is a treatise on poetics, Natyashastra is Bharata's treatise on dramaturgy, and the Mahabhashya is Patanjali's commentary on Panini's grammar.

items.value: Sanghabhuti wrote a commentary on the Sarvastivada Vinaya
items.reasoning: Sanghabhuti reached Chang'an in the early 380s CE and his known contribution to Chinese Buddhist literature is a Vinaya-vibhasha, a commentary on the monastic discipline of the Sarvastivada school, which was the dominant school in the north-western Indian regions from which such monks travelled. The others do not fit: the Visuddhimagga is itself Buddhaghosa's own fifth-century Theravada compendium composed in Sri Lanka, not a text an Indian monk in fourth-century China commented on; the Lalitavistara is a biography of the Buddha rather than a text carrying a well-known commentary of this period; and the major Chinese commentarial work on Prajnaparamita belongs to Kumarajiva's translation activity of the early fifth century. Runner-up is A (Prajnaparamita Sutra), which would win if the examiner has in mind the broader wave of Prajnaparamita commentary reaching China at the turn of the fifth century rather than Sanghabhuti's specific Vinaya work.

items.value: Only two of the four — Shantiniketan and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas — were inscribed in 2023
items.reasoning: India's two World Heritage inscriptions of 2023 were Shantiniketan in West Bengal and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (Belur, Halebid and Somanathapura) in Karnataka. Rani-ki-Vav, the stepwell at Patan in Gujarat, was inscribed in 2014, and the Mahabodhi Temple Complex at Bodh Gaya as long ago as 2002. So exactly two of the listed properties belong to 2023.

items.value: All three — Article 368 permits amendment by way of addition, variation and repeal
items.reasoning: Article 368(1) states that Parliament may in exercise of its constituent power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of the Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down in that Article. All three modes are named in the text itself, so the answer must include 1, 2 and 3.

items.value: Italy, Japan and South Korea are the three regularly in the news for low birth rates and ageing or shrinking populations
items.reasoning: Italy has one of Europe's lowest fertility rates and an outright declining population; Japan is the standard example of a super-aged and shrinking society; and South Korea has repeatedly recorded the lowest total fertility rate in the world, falling below 0.8. Nigeria and South Africa are the opposite case — Nigeria has one of the world's highest fertility rates and a very young, fast-growing population, and South Africa likewise has a young age structure and a growing population. So only 1, 2 and 4 fit.

items.value: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct; the Lok Sabha is not bound to accept the Rajya Sabha's recommendations on a Money Bill
items.reasoning: Article 109 is headed 'Special procedure in respect of Money Bills', so statement 1 is correct, and Article 109(1) read with Article 117(1) requires that a Money Bill be introduced only in the House of the People, so statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct as well: the Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within fourteen days with or without recommendations and cannot reject or amend it. Statement 4 is the false one — Article 109(3) expressly allows the Lok Sabha to accept or reject all or any of the Rajya Sabha's recommendations, so they do not have to be accepted.

items.value: Only row 3 — Major, Squadron Leader and Lieutenant Commander are the equivalent ranks
items.reasoning: Row 3 is correct: Major in the Army corresponds to Squadron Leader in the Air Force and Lieutenant Commander in the Navy. Row 1 is wrong because the naval equivalent of Brigadier and Air Commodore is Commodore, not Commander. Row 2 is wrong because Major General and Air Vice Marshal correspond to Rear Admiral; Vice Admiral matches Lieutenant General and Air Marshal. Row 4 is wrong because Lieutenant Colonel matches Wing Commander and Commander, whereas Group Captain and Captain (IN) both correspond to Colonel. With only row 3 standing, the answer is 3 only.

items.value: The Council comprises the Governor and the Chief Minister of each constituent State together with three members nominated by the President
items.reasoning: Section 3 of the North Eastern Council Act, 1971 as it stands after the 2002 amendment constitutes the Council of the Governor of each constituent State, the Chief Minister of each constituent State, and three members nominated by the President of India — the 2002 amendment's substantive changes were the addition of Sikkim as a constituent State and the recasting of the Council as a regional planning body. The Union Home Minister is not a statutory member under that section; his association with the Council as its Chairman came much later, through a government decision of 2018, and not through the 2002 amendment the stem anchors on. Runner-up is D, which would win if the examiner reads 'subsequent to the amendment of NEC Act in 2002' loosely as 'as the Council stands today' and therefore counts the Home Minister, who now chairs it.

items.value: Four Delimitation Commissions have been constituted — in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002
items.reasoning: Delimitation Commissions have been set up four times under Acts of Parliament: in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002. No further Commission of that general kind had been constituted up to December 2023, since delimitation of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies on the basis of population stands frozen until the first census after 2026 by the Eighty-fourth and Eighty-seventh Amendments. The 2020 Commission for Jammu and Kashmir and the North-Eastern States was a special exercise carried out under the Delimitation Act, 2002 rather than a fifth Commission in this series.

items.value: Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added by the 71st Amendment Act, 1992
items.reasoning: The Constitution (Seventy-first Amendment) Act, 1992 inserted three languages — Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali — into the Eighth Schedule, taking the total from fifteen to eighteen. Maithili does not belong here: it was added later, by the Constitution (Ninety-second Amendment) Act, 2003, together with Bodo, Dogri and Santhali, which took the total to twenty-two. So only 1, 2 and 3 are correct.

items.value: Only two pairs are correct — Bharatiya Jana Sangh with Shyama Prasad Mukherjee and Congress for Democracy with Jagjivan Ram
items.reasoning: Pair 1 is correct: Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee founded the Bharatiya Jana Sangh in 1951. Pair 3 is correct: the Congress for Democracy was formed in early 1977 by Jagjivan Ram, who broke from the Congress on the eve of the post-Emergency election. The other two are crossed over: the Swatantra Party was founded by C. Rajagopalachari in 1959, and Acharya Narendra Dev was a leader of the Congress Socialist Party and later the Socialist Party — so pair 2 wrongly attaches Rajagopalachari to the Socialist Party and pair 4 wrongly attaches Narendra Dev to Swatantra. Two correct pairs.

items.value: All three are correct — Municipalities in Part IX A, emergency provisions in Part XVIII, and amendment of the Constitution in Part XX
items.reasoning: Part IX A, inserted by the Seventy-fourth Amendment, covers the Municipalities in Articles 243P to 243ZG, including their powers and authority, so statement 1 is correct. Part XVIII contains the emergency provisions in Articles 352 to 360, so statement 2 is correct. Part XX consists of Article 368 on amendment of the Constitution, so statement 3 is correct as well. All three hold.

items.value: Inter-State quarantine is a Union subject in the Union List
items.reasoning: Entry 81 of the Union List reads 'Inter-State migration; inter-State quarantine', which makes option C correct and simultaneously falsifies option B, since inter-State migration is a Union and not a State subject. Option A fails because Entry 42 of the Union List covers inter-State trade and commerce, the State List (Entry 26) being confined to trade and commerce within the State. Option D fails because corporation tax appears at Entry 85 of the Union List.
